note: The components the contract defines. The web profile's components.css used to
be written by hand, which meant the styles a consumer shipped and the
contract behind it were two things that could disagree. The stylesheet is
now projected from this file, by a renderer that is generic: a component is
added by stating it here, not by adding a case to the renderer.
The names come from a measurement, not from a preference. The field was
walked and the components it declares were counted by lineage, and the
names that two or more independent lineages already agree on are the ones
declared here. The measurement is profiles/frontend-audit/CONVERGENCE.md and
it is regenerated by tools/component_convergence.py.
A component is stated by the roles it carries, the states it has, the tokens
it uses and the accessibility it owes. The tokens are roles, not colours: a
component says what a thing is for, and core/ROLES.json says what that is
worth on each substrate.

system.description: The typographic and numeric system a surface sits in: the family, the tabular numerals that make terse metadata line up, and the measure of a line of reading text.
note: The measure is 68 characters. A line of reading text that runs past it
is a line the eye loses: the return sweep starts in the wrong place.

button.description: The control a person presses. A disabled button is still readable, and the focus ring is visible without hover.

variants.name: primary
variants.description: The principal operation of the context. The system spends its one accent here, and a view has one of these.

variants.name: secondary
variants.description: A supporting operation: present, findable, and clearly not the principal one.

variants.name: quiet
variants.description: An operation that sits in the text of a surface rather than on it.

variants.name: destructive
variants.description: An operation with a material negative consequence. It never wears the accent, because the accent means the principal operation.

note: The text on the accent is anthracite, not white. Both pairings are approved and the white one measures 2.87 against Signal Orange, which is below AA for body text; the anthracite one measures 6.43. COL-002 asks for white on Signal Orange and WCAG exempts the text of an active control from the contrast requirement, so the rule is a floor and this is above it.
A destructive action wears the critical colour and never the accent, and its label says what will happen. A consequence is not carried by a colour alone.

text-input.description: A field a person types into, with a visible label and a focus treatment that does not depend on hover.
note: The field does not carry its own placeholder as its only label. A placeholder disappears the moment a person types, and a field that has lost its label is a field nobody can check.

badge.description: A short mark that says what a thing is: its condition, its category, its count. It carries the condition as a shape and a word, never as a colour alone.

variants.name: stable
variants.description: A condition that is observed and is well.

variants.name: attention
variants.description: A condition that is observed and asks for inspection.

variants.name: breach
variants.description: A condition that is observed and is a failure.

variants.name: evidence
variants.description: The source of a claim, in terse metadata.

note: The approved green measures 4.09 against the light substrate, so it is not a background behind text. It is the mark: the pip beside the word. The tinted surface behind the word is a separate role.
The word is the condition. The pip is the cue that does not depend on reading it. A badge with no word is a decoration.

card.description: A raised surface that holds one thing: a record, a result, a summary.

dialog.description: A surface that interrupts to ask for something, and that takes the keyboard until it is answered.
note: The overlay is a dimming of the surface, not a colour of its own. A dialog that dims with a translucent black is carrying a second palette; the system's way to dim is the substrate's own darker step.

tooltip.description: A short explanation that appears beside the thing it explains and goes away when the pointer or the focus leaves.
note: A tooltip is not a label and it is not a message. It never carries an action, because a pointer cannot reach it, and it never carries the only copy of a fact.

select.description: A control that opens a list of choices and shows the one that is chosen.

tabs.description: A set of panels that share one subject, of which one is shown.
note: The selected tab is carried by a surface and an edge, and by the aria-selected state, and never by colour alone. Two tabs that differ only in hue are two tabs a reader cannot tell apart.

toaster.description: The place a transient message arrives, and the place it is read while it is there.
note: A message that reports a request is a statement about what was asked for, not about what happened. The words intended, observed and derived are distinct, and a toast that says done when the request is still in flight is claiming success prematurely.

toggle.description: A control that turns something on or off, and says which state it is in.
note: The state is the attribute, not the colour. A toggle that is on looks different from one that is off, and an assistive service is told which it is.

command-palette.description: A field that takes a command rather than a value, and a list of the commands it could be.

icon.description: A glyph from the ratified subset, at the size the system says, in the colour the surface says.
note: A glyph is drawn from assets/icons and from nowhere else. A character that looks like an icon is not one, and a hand-drawn path is not the ratified set.
An icon that carries meaning on its own needs a name. An icon that repeats a word beside it is decoration and takes aria-hidden.

section-heading.description: The heading of a section, with the number that says where the section sits and the action that applies to it.

note: The field's own vocabularies, and what each of their components is in
the system's terms. The gnu6-design package carries the g6-*
vocabulary, which the field uses and the system did not declare. This
is the translation.
There is a second one. The native shell has thirty-one arrangements of
its own — windows, trays, widgets, nested panels, the arrangements it
offers to an agent — and the system did not declare them either. They
are carried as a translation, by name and by shape. The shell has no
licence, so nothing of its implementation travels; what travels is the
fact that the field made these arrangements and what each one is for.
The package carries thirty-nine names of the field's and fourteen of the
system's, published under the same prefix: the package is the
contract's projection into the vocabulary the field writes in, and a
consumer that has adopted it has both without knowing which is which.
Three kinds of entry, and the difference matters:
a component  the system's own element, under its canonical name
a pattern    a composition the system states but does not declare as an
element, because it is an arrangement rather than a thing
a primitive  a thing the system's type, spacing or accessibility tier
governs, with no component of its own
The mapping is checked against the package: a name the package declares and
the contract does not classify is a failure, so the two cannot drift.

action.note: The field's own spelling of the system's button. The field's code converges on the system's name, so that name is the canonical one; what the sheet does with it is stated here.
differs: The sheet's action is the field's own button, and it is not the system's. It carries two of the system's four variants — quiet, and portal, which the system does not declare — where the system has primary, secondary and destructive.
It marks itself with a square, and the system declares no mark on the button.
It carries an arrow, and the system declares no part on the button.
It knows the pressed state, [aria-pressed='true'], which the system does not declare on the button.
It is disabled with [aria-disabled='true'] where the system takes :disabled; it is made busy with [aria-busy='true'], as the system does.

tokens.transition: background-color var(--g6-dur-1) linear, border-color var(--g6-dur-1) linear, color var(--g6-dur-1) linear, transform var(--g6-dur-1) var(--g6-ease-out)

section.note: The field's own spelling of the system's section-heading. The field's code converges on the system's name, so that name is the canonical one; what the sheet does with it is stated here.
differs: The sheet's section is the field's own section-heading. It is a heading and a note in two parts, where the system has a number, a title and an intro in four.
It carries the space above the section; the system's section-heading carries none.

state.note: The field's own spelling of the system's badge. The field's code converges on the system's name, so that name is the canonical one; what the sheet does with it is stated here.
differs: The sheet's state is the field's own badge. It carries three of the system's four conditions — stable, attention, breach — and two the system does not declare: empty and planned. The system's evidence condition is not in the sheet.
It draws its mark as a square of the current colour, where the system declares the mark as a token the badge carries.

The shell is not vendored here, so this is a record of what the field made and nothing checks it against the shell: the system has not adopted these arrangements, and the native profile still carries no vocabulary of its own.

brand.meaning: The mark and the name of a product. The lockup is the system's identity colour and its own type, in two parts: the mark and the word.

dia.meaning: A diagram. The system's own content, carried by the system's canvas, its surfaces and its identity colours. It reads what it contains: a diagram marks itself by the drawing it holds.

doc.meaning: A document region: prose with its own rules. Seven parts around the system's type — the navigation, the breadcrumbs, the metadata, the body, the table of contents, the footnotes and the menu.

empty.meaning: The state of a surface that has nothing in it yet. The system's measure, its strong rule and its radius, with a heading and a word inside it.

ext.meaning: A link out of the surface. The system's own third text, and nothing else.

facts.meaning: The facts of a claim, set out. The system's rule between them, and its own type.

figure.meaning: A figure with its caption. A bounded region with the system's surface, its rule and its radius, and the links and the scroll that belong to it.

files.meaning: A list of files. The system's surface and its rule, with the system's own type.

footer.meaning: The end of a surface: the links and the credit. The system's rule above them, and its own type, in three parts.

frame.meaning: The bounded region a surface sets its content in. The system's own measure and gutter, and nothing else.

goto.meaning: A jump to a named place. The system's own emphasis, its strong rule and its focus.

hero.meaning: The opening block of a surface: the title, the words and the actions. Three parts over the system's display type, its surfaces and its measures.

lang.meaning: The language switch. The system's own type and emphasis; the choice it offers is the system's.

ledger.meaning: A ledger of facts, with the values aligned. The system's surface and its rules, its tabular figures and its heading type, in nine parts: the index, the rail, the rows, the title, the description, the meta and the arrow.

tokens.transition: transform var(--g6-dur-2) var(--g6-ease-out), color var(--g6-dur-1) linear

masthead.meaning: The identity block of a surface: the mark, the name, and the words beside them. The system's gutter, its rules and its type, in four parts.

menu.meaning: A menu: a list of choices that opens over the surface. The system's surfaces, its rules, its radius and its type, in four parts: the groups, the items, the locked items and the label.

menu-anchor.meaning: The element a menu opens from. It carries no rule of its own: the system's focus and selection rules apply to it.

notice.meaning: A notice: a condition that asks for attention. The system's measure and its rules, with the system's second text inside it.

page.meaning: The frame of a page. It carries no colour and no type of its own: the arrangement is the whole of it.

prose.meaning: A run of reading text. The system's type tier, its measure and its surfaces — the largest arrangement in the sheet, and the one that is almost entirely type.

rules.selector: .g6-prose p, .g6-prose ul, .g6-prose ol, .g6-prose dl, .g6-prose table, .g6-prose pre, .g6-prose blockquote, .g6-prose details, .g6-prose figure

rail.meaning: The navigation rail of a surface: a column of the sections, with the active one marked. The system's surfaces, its rules, its radius, its focus and its stable state, in eight parts.

record.meaning: One record in a ledger. The system's measure and its rules, with the heading type and the links.

specimen.meaning: A specimen: a thing shown with its own description. The system's rules and its small type, in two parts: the frame and the caption. It declares one variable of its own, the tick it measures with.

study.meaning: A study unit: the chapters and the exercises. The system's surface, its strong rule and its radius, with the stable state and the semibold type.

tokens.transition: background-color var(--g6-dur-1) linear, border-color var(--g6-dur-1) linear

sysbar.meaning: The system bar at the top of a surface: the identity, the status and the language. The system's gutter, its rules and its type, in two parts: the inner region and the end.

sysmenu.meaning: The menu the system bar opens. The system's surfaces, its rules, its radius and its motion, in one part: the panel.

sysnav.meaning: The navigation inside the system bar. The system's identity colours, its type and its motion.

toc.meaning: The table of contents. The system's rule between the entries, with the title above them.

toc-inline.meaning: The table of contents, inline with the text. The system's measure, its rule and its radius, set in the system's own type.

display.meaning: The display type. The system's type tier, and the track it sets for it.

enter.meaning: The staggered entrance of a group's children. The system's motion tier, which states the meaning of motion and the reduced-motion equivalence; it is not a component.

label.meaning: A small label. The system's type tier, with the strong rule that separates it from what it labels.

lede.meaning: The standfirst under a title. The system's type tier, in the second text.

num.meaning: A number, aligned with the others. The system's type tier and its tabular figures.

skip.meaning: The link that skips to the content. The system's accessibility rules: it is seen when it is focused, and it comes first in the tab order.

visually-hidden.meaning: Text a screen reader carries and a screen does not show. The system's accessibility rules.
